clauses.reason: EO 13225 section 3 revokes orders that established committees that have terminated and whose work is completed, and item (c) lists "Executive Order 13090, as amended by Executive Order 13136," establishing the President's Commission on the Celebration of Women in American History. That names this order. Its section 5 states "This order shall be effective September 30, 2001.", so the first end is 2001-09-30. The amended report date is a deadline and not an end.

research_rationale:
EO 13136 (signed 1999-09-03; 64 FR 48931, Federal Register of 1999-09-08, FR Doc. 99-23508) was read in full in the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13136.txt. It is one paragraph that extends the life of the President's Commission on the Celebration of Women in American History by amending section 2(c) of EO 13090: it deletes the March 1, 1999 final-report date and inserts December 31, 2000. First end: EO 13225 (signed 2001-09-28; 66 FR 50291, Federal Register of 2001-10-03), section 3(c), revokes EO 13090, "as amended by Executive Order 13136," among orders that established committees that have terminated and whose work is completed; its section 5 states "This order shall be effective September 30, 2001." EO 13225 names this order. The report date in the amended section 2(c) is a deadline, not an end; the parent's section 3(d) ("The Commission shall terminate 60 days after the submission of" its final report) is an earlier candidate whose trigger date no held source supplies, so it is disclosed as a spent fact and the order stays on the books until the express revocation. The held text is the machine-extracted text layer of the official Federal Register PDF; the PDF page images are not held, so identity (printed number, title, signing date and FR Doc. number) was checked on the text layer against the census register row.

savings.reason: No savings or exception wording appears in section 3 or section 5 of EO 13225 for this order. The extended report date was a deadline for a Commission with no continuing existence after the revocation.
